name: Enterprise Delivery Endeavour
description: A mock method used to prototype the pattern orchestration diagram. Diagram-only: it carries patterns, pattern views and orchestrations, and deliberately omits the alpha state models a schema-valid document would require.

narrativeElements.name: Situation
narrativeElements.description: The circumstances the endeavour starts from.

patterns.name: Programme Shaping
patterns.description: Turning an intent into a funded, mandated programme.

patternViews.name: Mandate
patternViews.description: Sponsorship and authority are established.

patternViews.name: Business Case
patternViews.description: The investment is justified and sized.

patternViews.name: Mobilisation
patternViews.description: Teams, funding and governance are stood up.

patterns.name: Milestone Plan
patterns.description: The delivery spine of the programme, as four service-assessment phases.

patternViews.name: Discovery
patternViews.description: Understand the problem before committing to a solution.

patternViews.name: Alpha
patternViews.description: Prove the risky parts with throwaway work.

patternViews.name: Beta
patternViews.description: Build the real thing and run it with real users.

patternViews.name: Live
patternViews.description: Operate at full scale and keep improving.

patterns.name: Sprint
patterns.description: The team's delivery cycle, repeating until the phase objective is met.

patternViews.name: Plan
patternViews.description: Agree the sprint goal and the work that serves it.

patternViews.name: Build
patternViews.description: Produce a potentially releasable increment.

patternViews.name: Review
patternViews.description: Inspect the increment with stakeholders.

patternViews.name: Retrospective
patternViews.description: Inspect the way of working and adapt it.

patterns.name: Release Train
patterns.description: Moving an accepted increment into production on a fixed cadence.

patternViews.name: Integrate
patternViews.description: Assemble the increments into one release candidate.

patternViews.name: Harden
patternViews.description: Test, fix and freeze the candidate.

patternViews.name: Deploy
patternViews.description: Promote to production and verify in place.

patterns.name: Assurance and Governance
patterns.description: Independent oversight running for the whole life of delivery.

patternViews.name: Baseline
patternViews.description: Agree what good looks like and what will be checked.

patternViews.name: Stage Gate
patternViews.description: Review at each phase boundary and decide to continue.

patternViews.name: Audit
patternViews.description: Test the evidence independently of the delivery team.

patterns.name: Architecture Runway
patterns.description: Laying down enough technical foundation to stay ahead of delivery.

patternViews.name: Set Direction
patternViews.description: Choose the architectural approach and its constraints.

patternViews.name: Prove
patternViews.description: Demonstrate the approach against the riskiest requirement.

patternViews.name: Harden
patternViews.description: Make the foundation production-worthy.

patterns.name: Incident Response
patterns.description: What the team does when production is hurting.

patternViews.name: Detect
patternViews.description: Recognise and declare the incident.

patternViews.name: Contain
patternViews.description: Stop the harm spreading.

patternViews.name: Recover
patternViews.description: Restore normal service.

patternViews.name: Learn
patternViews.description: Find the cause and remove it.

patterns.name: Scope Change Control
patterns.description: Handling a change that the agreed plan does not accommodate.

patternViews.name: Raise
patternViews.description: Capture the proposed change and who wants it.

patternViews.name: Assess
patternViews.description: Size the impact on cost, time and risk.

patternViews.name: Decide
patternViews.description: Accept, reject or defer, and tell everyone affected.

patterns.name: Benefits Realisation
patterns.description: Finding out whether the programme actually produced what it promised.

patternViews.name: Measure
patternViews.description: Collect the outcome data the business case named.

patternViews.name: Compare
patternViews.description: Set actuals against the forecast.

patternViews.name: Report
patternViews.description: Tell the sponsor what was and was not achieved.

patterns.name: Programme Closure
patterns.description: Ending the programme deliberately rather than letting it fade.

patternViews.name: Handover
patternViews.description: Transfer ownership to the teams that will run it.

patternViews.name: Decommission
patternViews.description: Retire what the programme stood up and no longer needs.

patternViews.name: Close
patternViews.description: Release the people and shut the governance down.

patternOrchestrations.name: Enterprise Delivery Endeavour
patternOrchestrations.description: The whole shape of a funded programme: shaping, delivery with assurance alongside and sprints inside, then benefits and closure.

exitCriteria.name: Programme is mandated and funded
exitCriteria.description: Whether the programme has the authority and money to proceed.
given: a business case has been prepared
then: funding is released and a sponsor is named

narrativeContexts.context: An intent exists but nothing is funded, staffed or mandated.

entryCriteria.description: A sponsor, a funded business case and a mobilised delivery team are in place before any phase starts.

exitCriteria.name: Service is live and supported
exitCriteria.description: Whether the service can be run by the people who will own it.
given: the service has been through a live assessment
when: the operating team takes the pager
then: the service runs without the delivery team on standby

narrativeContexts.context: Deliver a service that meets the need the business case identified.
Four phases of increasing commitment, each one earning the right to the next.

entryCriteria.description: The service has been live long enough for outcome data to mean something.

exitCriteria.name: Benefits are evidenced
exitCriteria.description: Whether the promised outcomes can be shown to have happened.
given: the service has been live for a full reporting period
when: actuals are compared against the business case forecast
then: the variance is explained and accepted by the sponsor

narrativeContexts.context: The forecast in the business case is tested against what actually happened.
The programme ends deliberately, with ownership transferred and governance shut down.

exitCriteria.name: Every gate has a recorded decision
exitCriteria.description: Whether oversight kept up with delivery.
given: the plan has passed its final phase boundary
then: each phase boundary carries a dated continue-or-stop decision

exitCriteria.name: Increment accepted
exitCriteria.description: Whether the increment met the phase objective it was serving.
given: a sprint has run to its end
when: the increment is reviewed against the phase objective
then: the increment is accepted or its shortfall carries into the next sprint

entryCriteria.name: Standing team available to the phase
entryCriteria.description: Whether a product team exists to carry the phase rather than the programme staffing it anew.
given: a phase of the milestone plan has been opened
when: a standing product team is assigned to it
then: that team's own rhythm runs inside the phase rather than the programme scheduling its sprints

exitCriteria.name: Phase objective met by the team
exitCriteria.description: Whether the embedded rhythm delivered what the phase asked of it.
given: the embedded rhythm has been running for the phase
then: the phase closes or its shortfall carries into the next one

trigger.name: Production impact recognised
trigger.description: What the team notices that causes the incident pattern to be run.
given: the service is carrying production traffic
when: a user-visible failure is recognised by anyone on the team
then: the incident response pattern is entered regardless of the phase in progress

trigger.name: Change outside the agreed plan
trigger.description: What causes the change pattern to be run rather than absorbed.
when: a stakeholder asks for something the plan does not accommodate
then: the change is raised formally rather than absorbed into the next sprint

patternOrchestrations.name: Product Team Operating Rhythm
patternOrchestrations.description: The same sprint and incident patterns, reused by a standing product team with no programme around them.

exitCriteria.name: Increment released
exitCriteria.description: Whether the cycle ended with something in users' hands.
given: a sprint has run to its end
then: it is released or explicitly held with a reason

trigger.name: Production impact recognised
trigger.description: What the team notices that interrupts the rhythm.
then: the sprint is interrupted and the incident pattern is entered
